title: Derived tensor, pullback and direct-image comparisons for a scheme-isomorphism square
statement: Let X,Y,X',Y' be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with chosen derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] of X,Y in a common morphism universe w and of X',Y' in a common independently chosen universe w'. Use the recorded tensors [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], pullbacks [def-pc-derived-pullback] and direct images [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Let f:X\to Y, g:X'\to Y', e_X:X'\cong X, e_Y:Y'\cong Y satisfy g;e_Y=e_X;f. Let a:D(Y')\simeq D(Y), b:D(X')\simeq D(X) be supplied equivalences, together with natural isomorphisms Q;a \cong (e_Y)_*^{complex};Q and Q;b \cong (e_X)_*^{complex};Q. Here Q is complex localization and the complex functors apply underived module pushforward in every degree and to every differential. Then there are natural isomorphisms tensor_{Y'};a \cong (a\times a);tensor_Y, tensor_{X'};b \cong (b\times b);tensor_X, a;Lf^* \cong Lg^*;b, and Rg_*;a \cong b;Rf_*. There are no supplied adjunctions, tensor-pullback comparisons, coefficients, quasi-coherence assumptions, or projection-mate assertions.

proof.text: Construct the explicit module equivalence for a scheme isomorphism s from pushforward along s.hom and s.inv, using pushforwardComp, pushforwardCongr and pushforwardId for its unit and counit. Its forward functor F is exact. The exact-functor localization factorization identifies the supplied a.functor with F.mapDerivedCategory by Localization.liftNatIso. The inverse localization comparison for F is a right-derived unit, so right-derived uniqueness (the proved source interface F.rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory) identifies this with schemeDerivedDirectImage s.hom. Apply the proved private iso_directImage helper to eX and eY.

For each s and supplied equivalence a, take the existing strong-monoidal pullback-across-universes functor L and its adjunction to schemeDerivedDirectImage s.hom. Transport its right side through iso_directImage to obtain L adjoint to a.functor. Since a.functor is an equivalence, this adjunction upgrades to an equivalence whose forward functor is L and inverse is a.functor. Equivalence.inverseMonoidal makes that inverse strong monoidal. Its inverse tensorator Functor.Monoidal.muNatIso.symm gives the tensor comparison. Apply this construction to eY,a,ha and eX,b,hb.

Use derivedDirectImageComposition for g,eY.hom and eX.hom,f. Whisker the eY identification on the left by Rg, follow by the inverse g;eY composition comparison, transport along hcomm by eqToIso, then follow by the eX;f comparison and whisker the inverse eX identification on the right by Rf. This constructs beta: Rg followed by a.functor is isomorphic to b.functor followed by Rf.

Take the existing adjunctions Lf adjoint to Rf and Lg adjoint to Rg. Compose the latter after a.inverse adjoint to a.functor, and the former before b.inverse adjoint to b.functor. Mathlib conjugateIsoEquiv applied inversely to beta yields delta: Lf followed by b.inverse is isomorphic to a.inverse followed by Lg. Prewhisker delta by a.functor and postwhisker by b.functor, cancelling a.functor;a.inverse with a.unitIso.symm and b.inverse;b.functor with b.counitIso. The explicit associator/unitor chain in pullback_comparison yields a.functor;Lf isomorphic to Lg;b.functor. Pair the two tensor comparisons, this pullback comparison and beta. All constructions use only supplied localizations and work for independent morphism universes and empty schemes.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08EU scheme-isomorphism transport, implemented using the existing derived adjunction of Tag 079W, the monoidal pullback comparison of Tag 079U, and direct-image composition of Tag 0D5T. Tensor preservation follows by inverting a monoidal equivalence; pullback-square transport follows by conjugating the direct-image-square comparison.

theorem schemeIso_derived_functor_comparisons
    (X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X'.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y'.toRingedSpace))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : X' ⟶ Y') (eX : X' ≅ X) (eY : Y' ≅ Y)
    (hcomm : g ≫ eY.hom = eX.hom ≫ f)
    (a : schemeDerivedCategory Y' ≌ schemeDerivedCategory Y)
    (b : schemeDerivedCategory X' ≌ schemeDerivedCategory X)
    (ha : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ a.functor ≅
      (@Functor.mapHomologicalComplex ℤ
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y'.toRingedSpace))
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) _ _ _ _
        (SheafOfModules.pushforward eY.hom.toRingCatSheafHom)
        ⟨fun _ _ ↦ rfl⟩ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (hb : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ b.functor ≅
      (@Functor.mapHomologicalComplex ℤ
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X'.toRingedSpace))
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) _ _ _ _
        (SheafOfModules.pushforward eX.hom.toRingCatSheafHom)
        ⟨fun _ _ ↦ rfl⟩ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q) :
    Nonempty (tensor (schemeDerivedCategory Y') ⋙ a.functor ≅
      a.functor.prod a.functor ⋙ tensor (schemeDerivedCategory Y)) ∧
    Nonempty (tensor (schemeDerivedCategory X') ⋙ b.functor ≅
      b.functor.prod b.functor ⋙ tensor (schemeDerivedCategory X)) ∧
    Nonempty (a.functor ⋙ derivedPullback f ≅ derivedPullback g ⋙ b.functor) ∧
    Nonempty (schemeDerivedDirectImage g ⋙ a.functor ≅
      b.functor ⋙ schemeDerivedDirectImage f)
